criteria: A build that uses a `filter` with `options.outputReferences: outputReferencesFilter`, where the filter excludes tokens that the remaining tokens reference, completes without printing the "filtered out token references were found" warning — at both default and verbose verbosity.

In that build the generated file content is unchanged: tokens whose references were filtered out are still emitted as fully resolved literal values, with no `var(...)` (or format-equivalent reference) pointing at an excluded token.
The warning does not appear when the excluded token is at the end of a multi-level chain, e.g. a kept token references another kept token that references an excluded token.

A genuine case still warns: with `options.outputReferences: true` (not the filter function) and a filter that excludes referenced tokens, the "filtered out token references were found" warning is still reported.
When `outputReferencesFilter` is used, emitted tokens remain reference-safe ordered — a kept token is declared before any kept token that references it.
description:
When a file uses a `filter` together with `options.outputReferences: outputReferencesFilter`, Style Dictionary can still print the warning "While building <file>, filtered out token references were found; output may be unexpected" even though the generated file contains no references at all and every value is fully resolved. The warning is a false positive: outputReferencesFilter did its job and suppressed the references, but a warning for a filtered-out reference was left behind in the global message collector and was never cleared.

Expected behavior: if outputReferencesFilter suppresses all references for a token, no "filtered out token references were found" warning is reported for that file.

Root cause: reference warnings are tracked in a global collector and are removed on the honor system — each formatted token removes the warnings for the references in its own original value. The internal reference-safety sort runs whenever `outputReferences` is truthy, and the `outputReferencesFilter` function is truthy, so the sort runs too. The sort probes references with `warnImmediately: false` and records a "filtered out reference" warning for any reference that only resolves through the unfiltered token set, but it never removes those warnings. It also recurses into the referenced tokens when ordering, so it can scan tokens that are themselves filtered out of the file; those tokens are never formatted, so outputReferencesFilter never visits them and their warnings are never cleared. The accumulated leftover warnings then make the file look like it still emits references to filtered-out tokens. This is data-dependent (which tokens get compared, and whether the sort recurses into a filtered-out token, depends on the filtered token set), which is why removing tokens from a token file can make the warning disappear.
